featured_reviews.name: Sheldon Dias
featured_reviews.review_text:
Located in the St. Pauls Media Complex, St Paul Book And Art Centre Mumbai is a serene landmark that serves as a one-stop destination for spiritual literature and religious artifacts. It is particularly well-regarded for its peaceful, library-like atmosphere, offering a quiet refuge for visitors to browse through a wide range of specialized materials.
• Diverse Collection: The store is a major hub for religious and spiritual books, including Bibles in various editions, theological texts, and Catholic literature, as well as academic titles, CBSE textbooks, and children's storybooks.
• Art and Gifts: Beyond literature, it features an extensive selection of religious artifacts, such as statues, rosaries, candles, and framed prints, making it a popular spot for meaningful gifts and church supplies.
• Holiday Highlights: During the Christmas season, the first floor transforms into a festive destination stocked with unique décor, souvenirs, and seasonal ornaments.
• Supportive Environment: Visitors frequently mention the well-organized layout and the helpful, professional staff who are knowledgeable about the inventory and assist with niche title requests.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Then we walked into Crosswords bookstore right next door and realized Third Wave is inside the store, near the counter. There is a decent seating area there, not huge, but enough space to sit comfortably with a coffee.

The bookstore itself is nice. It’s spacious and has a wide range of books and other products. You’ll find books across many genres, along with stationery and gift items. Prices vary a lot. Some books are affordable, while others, especially imported editions, are quite expensive. It really depends on what you pick up and where it’s coming from.

I liked that there were options at different price points. You can browse without feeling rushed, and it doesn’t feel too cramped even when there are people around. The coffee inside makes it a good place to pause for a bit, read a few pages, or just sit quietly.

We were actually looking for Third Wave Coffee and found it on the map. When we reached the building, there was no sign of it anywhere. Nothing in the elevator either, so we were a bit confused at first

Overall, it’s a good bookstore to visit in Juhu if you enjoy browsing and don’t mind spending some time there. Just know that Third Wave Coffee is inside Crosswords and not a separate outlet, which can be confusing at first.

featured_reviews.name: Rajesh Jagtap
featured_reviews.review_text:
An absolutely well thought off idea about renting out kids toys, books and other fun products. The library is exactly as you must seen or heard. It is economical compared to buying toys for your baby, toddler or kids who play with it only for a limited time as they continue to grow. So it’s better to keep the toys changing at regular intervals so that kids are also engaged. You get toys, books, charts, etc starting from 6 months babies to 6 year old kids. You will also find pregnancy related books and activities to do here as well. Since it’s a library you have to return or re-register the things you have taken every 15 days. Talking about the owners, the couple have done courses related to child growth and child care and hence are very well versed with the library and it’s contents. The staff is also very good knowledge of the products inside the library and give very good suggestions. Everyone is super friendly. The quality of the toys are also good and it’s a well kept, clean place.
